title: Quotient Rule in Action
caption_md: The blue curve is $Q(x) = \frac{x^2}{\sin x}$, the example from the lesson. The dashed tangent line at $x = 1$ has slope given by the Quotient Rule: $$Q'(x) = \frac{2x\,\sin x - x^2\,\cos x}{\sin^2 x}.$$ At $x=1$ this evaluates to $Q'(1) \approx 1.53$. The orange dashed curve is the derivative $Q'(x)$ itself. Notice how the tangent line's slope matches the height of the orange curve at $x=1$. Verify that swapping the subtraction order (the most common mistake) would give you the wrong sign for the slope.
